meta.title: Isometric projection geometry and piping-isometric drawing conventions
meta.note: Closed forms are exact; conventions are trade practice (no clause of the paywalled ISO 6412-2 text was read). Each row names its source id from ../sources.md.

closedForms.quantity: angle between any two projected axes
foreshortening of every axis (true isometric projection)

llullIsoFrame.definition: iso: right = unit(1, 1, 0); up = unit(cross(unit(1, -1, 1), right)); viewer at (+X, -Y, +Z)
llullIsoFrame.derivation: pcf_reference_parse.py iso_axes(); plant north (+Y) projects up-right at +30 deg, which is the preferred north-arrow direction on piping isometrics (S20).

conventions.rule: Isometrics are not drawn to scale; lengths are written as dimensions
North arrow pointing up-right is preferred; up-left is the alternative; it rarely if ever points down
Dimensions are taken from the pipe centreline (centre of fittings / face of flanges), not from the outside diameter
Horizontal positions are given by coordinates, vertical ones by elevations (EL)
Slopes are marked on the pipe with a ratio (e.g. SLOPE 1:100) and an arrow showing the fall direction

Lines not parallel to an isometric axis are skews / offsets: drawn inside a hatched 'squaring-in' triangle or box; a 45 deg offset is drawn at 22.5 deg from the axis so it does not read as an axis line
Shop welds, field (site) welds and field-fit welds use different symbols (SKEY WW / WS / WF); field welds split spools
Isometric tables: bill of materials, cut piece list, weld list, spool list
Isometric styles in Plant 3D: check, stress, final (with BOM, document of record), spool
A large isometric is split over several sheets; continuation is marked at the split point and sheet content is kept stable across re-issues (Smart 3D: overflow goes to a new sheet '1A')
Spool size limit is a project / shipping rule (cube size, weight or model property in Plant 3D); ASME B31.3 sets no maximum spool length
A field-fit weld adds a user-set allowance to the calculated cut length of the adjoining pipe (ISODRAFT)
Spool numbers run continuously from one drawing to the next by default; weld numbers not stored in the database are not kept between revisions (ISODRAFT)

standards.title: Technical product documentation - Simplified representation of pipelines - Part 1: General rules and orthogonal representation
standards.facts: edition 2, 2017-12, confirmed 2023, replaces ISO 6412-1:1989; applies to all kinds of pipes and pipelines, rigid or flexible, any material; can be used for ventilation / air-conditioning ducts

standards.title: Technical product documentation - Simplified representation of pipelines - Part 2: Isometric projection
standards.facts: edition 2, 2017-12, 12 pages, confirmed 2023, replaces ISO 6412-2:1989, ISO/TC 10/SC 10; supplementary rules to Part 1 for isometric representation, used where essential features must be shown clearly in three dimensions
